explanations.treaty-of-tordesillas-1494--portuguese-l: Cabral did not sail to find Brazil and the treaty did not send him; what the treaty did was decide in advance what a landfall there would mean. Taking possession in the name of Manuel I was an act with a legal addressee — Castile — and it worked because the coast lay east of the meridian agreed six years earlier. The claim here is narrow and is the weakest of the five types on purpose: the line did not cause the voyage, it is what made the voyage a claim.
explanations.treaty-of-tordesillas-1494--the-atlantic: The treaty is usually read for what it gave Portugal in the west. Read for what it left in the east it is the other half of the same fact: everything on the African side of the meridian stayed Portuguese, the Guinea and Angola coasts included. One crown therefore held both ends of a traffic that had not begun yet — the ports the captives were embarked at and the coast they were landed on. Wikipedia’s account of the Brazilian trade has most of the five and a half million embarking at West Central African ports, above all Luanda; that they were Portuguese ports is what 1494 settled.
